rv.q: This production of Little Shop of Horrors is an absolute triumph and thoroughly deserving of its five-star rating.

Howard Ashman and Alan Menken’s gloriously twisted musical swallows up the tiny stage at Hope Mill Theatre and spits out a production that is big on personality, generous with laughs and positively blooming with lush performances from all the cast.
It's just a joyful night at the theatre.
It’s easy to enjoy being caught in its fangs.
With its infectious score and sharp humour, this production is one that understands exactly what makes this musical so enduring.
Overall, this production is a triumph perfectly scaled to the intimacy of the Hope Mill Theatre, though it would imaginably delight audiences on a larger stage as well.
The cult horror-comedy musical is back at Manchester's Hope Mill Theatre, and it's an absolute blast.

cn.t: Critics hail this Hope Mill production as a triumph, with near-universal praise for its polished execution and wickedly funny performances. The carnivorous Audrey II steals the show, while Benjamin Yates' sadistic dentist earns standout acclaim.
